title: internal/exec/subprocess's processAlive reads unreaped zombies as alive inside the factory container
body: process_unix.go's processAlive is the same signal-0 shape fixed for the gate test in tick 58z: kill(pid, 0) succeeds on a zombie, and the factory container's PID 1 never reaps, so a killed legacy attempt's pid reads as alive there forever. It is used by cancel.go's stopTree (the stop-tree poll waits on it) and inspect.go's alive(), both on the LEGACY pre-lock paths only (tick rmc moved liveness to locks for everything newer), which is why it is low severity — but the same zombie-blindness the container just exposed for the gate applies to it verbatim.
